items.title: Lemon Nash Interview, 1959-10-03
items.q: We all played together. He played violin.

ctx.x: Does he live around Scotlandville or close in than that?

No, he don't live very far from Louisa Street. It's a fella got a place out there in Baton Rouge they call the APEC. It's a ballroom. Anybody in that APEC that you ever catch in the APEC going to show you where Sa Youn lives. Sa Youn don't live far from that. Well he's one of the old violin players of New Orleans. We all played together. He played violin. We had a violin, ukulele, and I had another boy who played a mandolin with me, Johnny Bynum. He died in Baton Rouge. He and I traveled all over together…
Let me turn it off a second. You tell him about you played with Sa Youn and Bynum was with you? Mm-hmm. And all that, okay? Yeah. And then what happened?

items.title: Lemon Nash Interview, 1959-10-03
items.q: There's La Youn, the violin player. He lived in Baton Rouge.

ctx.x: Let's see, after you worked with August, who did you work with?

Well, after I worked with August, I worked with Cyun, a violin player. He's an old timer too. He lived in Baton Rouge, you know. We used to play all out of the canal in front, that Eddie Woodruff place. You know where he is? Walter Coren, the one that had the position in the custom house. We used to play for all their parties. They used to throw on big parties. There's La Youn, the violin player. He lived in Baton Rouge.
What part of Baton Rouge does he live in?
